test_title: PYST 2: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Change the following from active to passive:

The jury had announced the final verdict after a thorough discussion.

options.text: The final verdict was being announced after a thorough discussion.
The final verdict had been announced by the jury after a thorough discussion.
The final verdict is announced after a thorough discussion.
The final verdict was announced after a thorough discussion.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The jury had announced the final verdict after a thorough discussion."
 
• This sentence is in the **Past Perfect** tense (had + V3). The rule for conversion to passive is: *Object + had + been + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject.*
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "The final verdict" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb "had announced" to "had been announced."
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the jury."
 
• The phrase "after a thorough discussion" remains at the end to provide context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The final verdict had been announced by the jury after a thorough discussion."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The final verdict was being announced..." – Incorrect because it uses the Past Continuous passive form.
 
• **Option 3: **"The final verdict is announced..." – Incorrect because it uses the Present Simple passive form.
 
• **Option 4: **"The final verdict was announced..." – Incorrect because it uses the Past Simple passive form.
